house_rules: Every proof routes through the operator's declared canary collector (scope.csv class canary, http_probe with canary=True) - a DNS log or HTTP hit on a third-party service is gossip, not channel proof (organ doctrine).
Payloads below are canonical forms from the public record, attributed per entry.
Egress toward cloud metadata endpoints is an authorized-only action: the scope row must cover the HOST the request actually lands on, not just the URL the parameter names.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a bypass that failed for a listed reason leaves the filter untested, not effective.

prerequisites: sink fetches attacker-named URLs with a permissive scheme handler
entries.oracle: file contents in the response body or a body-hash differential vs a nonexistent path
failure_modes: scheme allowlist (http/https only) - the refusal itself is a FACT about the sink's validation posture
response body never surfaced - pair with a canary-readable transform (error text, size oracle) instead of assuming failure

prerequisites: gopher handler reachable in the sink's URL stack
internal TCP service (Redis/MySQL/SMTP) in egress reach
entries.oracle: the internal service state changes / answers - Redis MONITOR or the service's observable side effect is the proof; bounded to a self-owned proof key
failure_modes: gopher stripped by URL validation - try gophers:// or the secondary handlers (dict://, ftp://) before closing
egress firewall drops the port regardless of scheme
the proof must be reversible (DEL the proof key) - never leave state on client infrastructure

entries.technique: operator canary channel proof (the house entry)
prerequisites: scope.csv row class canary for the operator collector (with artifact)
http_probe(canary=True) route
entries.probe: payload URL host pointing at the declared collector: https://{{collector}}/collect/{{marker}} - the SSRF itself places the URL in the sink parameter
entries.oracle: a GET poll on the collector (canary mode: GET-only, no query string, bounded path) returns the marker - the CHANNEL is proven end-to-end: server-side request -> collector -> operator poll, every hop ledgered CANARY
failure_modes: the canary gate refuses the URL (query string or path slack) - that refusal is doctrine working, re-shape the payload within the channel rules
no callback after differential says the fetch happened - egress filtering between sink and collector; try the redirect entry (SSRF-004) as the delivery path
a third-party interaction host responding instead of the operator collector = gossip, never a CONFIRMED channel record

entries.technique: IPv6 loopback family (bracket notations and IPv6 names)
prerequisites: filter matches IPv4 literal forms only
the sink's URL stack resolves IPv6
entries.probe: http://[::]:80/ (unspecified) / http://[0000::1]:80/ (long loopback) / http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/ (IPv4-mapped) / http://ip6-localhost/ (host form of ::1)
entries.oracle: the request lands on the loopback the filter missed - canary callback (SSRF-010) or response differential proves resolution; each bracket form is its own FACT row, never one class
failure_modes: the sink's resolver rejects bracket forms (RFC 3986 host parsing varies per library) - ledger the library pair, the same law as SSRF-009
IPv6 entirely absent on the internal network - the family closes as a FACT, not a negative for the whole organ
ip6-localhost naming absent from the sink's resolver hosts file - the name form fails while bracket forms may still answer

entries.technique: AWS IMDSv2 session-token dance (PUT + TTL header through the SSRF)
prerequisites: SSRF egress to 169.254.169.254 from an AWS workload
IMDSv2 enforced (bare-GET IMDSv1 closed — SSRF-006 already returned 401)
the sink can be driven to issue a PUT with a caller-named header — method control plus header control is the class gate (the appsecco record names both requirements)
entries.probe: PUT /latest/api/token with header X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600 mints the session token; every subsequent metadata GET carries header X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: <token> — canonical record: TOKEN=`curl -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600"` && curl -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/dynamic/instance-identity/ (IPv6 form on the same record: http://[fd00:ec2::254]/latest/meta-data/)
entries.oracle: the second GET answers 200 with metadata content where the bare GET answered 401 — the token dance succeeded THROUGH the sink; any credential material in the response follows the SSRF-006 masking law (first 8 chars in the ledger, full value only in the engagements/ artifact)
failure_modes: sink issues GET-only (vanilla URL-parameter SSRF) — the class is closed at that sink and IMDSv2 is doing its job; record the hardening as a positive FACT, do not keep firing
hop limit 1 (the default) — containerized workers one NAT hop away get the token PUT refused; the limit is a knob, not a wall
PUT requests carrying an X-Forwarded-For header are rejected by IMDSv2 (documented refusal) — proxy-shaped sinks fail here for a documented reason
TTL above 21600 seconds is not honored — the record's own six-hour cap; treat oversized TTL probes as malformed, not as evidence

prerequisites: egress to 169.254.169.254 from an Azure workload with a managed identity attached
the sink can send the Metadata: true header — plain GETs are refused, the header is the gate (SSRF-008's fingerprint in reverse)
entries.oracle: 200 with a JSON access_token for the named resource — credential-bearing response: mask at first 8 chars in the ledger, full value only in the engagements/ artifact; an identity error or empty block means no managed identity on the workload and the class closes as exposure-only
failure_modes: no managed identity attached — the endpoint answers with an identity error; bounded to information disclosure, say so
the sink cannot set arbitrary headers — header injection via the URL is a separate hypothesis (SSRF-009's parser seam), never an assumption
the resource parameter is part of the byte record: api-version=2018-02-01 and the %2F-encoded resource URL — a raw-slash form is a different request, ledger it separately or not at all
